gloss: have no recourse; nothing can be done; at a loss

definitions.gloss: have no recourse; nothing can be done; no way to deal with it
definitions.explanation: An expression meaning there are no available measures or strategies to resolve a problem. Literally 'there is no move to play,' from the game of go or shogi.

examples.japanese: もう{打|う}つ{手|て}がない。
examples.english: There's nothing more we can do.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}は{打|う}つ{手|て}がないと{言|い}った。
examples.english: The doctor said nothing more could be done.

examples.japanese: {赤字|あかじ}が{続|つづ}き、{経営陣|けいえいじん}は{打|う}つ{手|て}がない{状態|じょうたい}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: Losses continued, and the management was driven into a state where nothing could be done.

notes:
Literally "there is no move to play" — a metaphor from board games (go, shogi) where no viable move remains. Expresses helplessness in the face of a problem that cannot be solved.

FORMS:
- {打|う}つ{手|て}がなくなる: to run out of options
- {打|う}つ{手|て}なし: no recourse (more concise form)
- {打|う}つ{手|て}を{失|うしな}う: to lose all options

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手|て}の{施|ほどこ}しようがない: nothing can be done (more formal)
- お{手上|てあ}げ: throwing up one's hands; giving up
- {為|な}す{術|すべ}がない: there is nothing one can do (literary)

ETYMOLOGY:
From board game terminology — {打|う}つ{手|て} refers to a move or play one can make. When there are no more moves available, one has lost.
